title.narrative: Stöd till serbiska kommuner - SCTM och SALAR partnerskap.
Support to Serbian municipalities - SCTM and SALAR partnership

description.narrative:
Projektet är en treårig insats (2022 - 2025) för att stödja serbiska kommuner med det övergripande målet att förbereda dem inför EU-anslutningen, genom att skapa förbättrade förutsättningar för dem att tillhandahålla offentliga tjänster med hög kvalitet, och för stärkt dialog med intressenter och effektivare lokala förvaltningar, i enlighet med principerna om god förvaltning och jämställdhet.
Projektet kommer att bygga vidare på erfarenheterna från föregående fas och kommer att fortsätta ge stöd till utvalda kommuner genom MSP:er inom följande tematiska områden: 1) Miljö och klimat; 2) katastrofriskminskning (DRR); 3) Jämställdhet; och 4) Lokal ekonomisk utveckling, inklusive kvinnligt företagande.

The project is a three-year initiative (2022 - 2025) to support Serbian municipalities with the overall goal of preparing them for EU accession, by creating improved conditions for high-quality public services, and for strengthened dialogue with stakeholders and more efficient local administrations, in accordance with the principles of good administration and gender equality.
The project will build on the experiences from the previous phase and will continue to provide support to selected municipalities through MSPs in the following thematic areas: 1) Environment and climate; 2) Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR); 3) Gender Equality; and 4) Local economic development, including Women entrepreneurship.

The project will support Serbian Local Self-Governments (LSGs) to become more accountable and effective in delivering inclusive and higher quality services to all men, women, boys and girls in their constituencies, based on the principles of gender equality and the human rights-based approach. Partners intend to implement the same approach that was assessed as adequate and successful in the previous phase:
1) work with selected towns municipalities through MSPs (including municipal administrations, local public utility companies, inhabitants, civil society organizations (CSOs), academia) in order to strengthen their governance, strategic and operational management capacities as well as their ability to deliver improved, inclusive and sustainable public services.
2) building on experiences from earlier MSPs and making use of SCTMs networks and committees, the project will implement certain capacity development initiatives to increase capacities, awareness and understanding among a large number of LSGs.
3) The project will work towards more effective evidence-based advocacy and strategic dialogue with the national level based on LSGs needs, experiences and conditions in the four thematic areas.

description.narrative:
The project successfully implemented planned activities in both project components: 1) hands-on support to local self-governments (LSGs) provided through Municipal Support Packages (MSPs) and 2) overall support to local governments.
Some of the key achievements in the third project year with regards to the first component (MSPs) are the following:
- Within the thematic area of environmental protection, the project successfully completed five Municipal Support Packages (MSPs): three focused on Sustainable Urban Mobility Planning (SUMP) one on Circular economy, and one addressing air pollution. All three urban mobility plans were developed in full alignment with the relevant strategic and legal frameworks governing urban mobility. At the same time, the data collected through the preparation of the heating register provide a solid basis for introducing measures to reduce air pollution, decrease energy consumption, and enhance the efficiency of combustion devices in households, residential buildings, and private facilities.
- The gender equality support packages for Vrbas and Vrnjaka Banja have been successfully completed. These packages provided legal assistance in aligning gender equality mechanisms (such as the Gender Equality Council, Commission, and Officer) and resulted in the preparation of two legally mandated documents: Risk Management Plans for Gender Equality Violations and Local Action Plans (LAPs) for gender equality. Gender budgeting has been effectively introduced in both LSGs, with gender responsive goals and indicators incorporated into five budget programs. In addition, a series of workshops and working meetings were held to provide legal support, strengthen gender equality mechanisms, and facilitate the development of local action plans.
- All targeted LSGs for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR support) prepared Risk Assessment, Protection and Rescue Plans, and Disaster Risk Reduction Plans. These documents were developed with a strong focus on transparency and inclusiveness, particularly in key stages of the process such as communication and stakeholder consultation.
- Within Local Economic Development Women's Entrepreneurship MSPs the City of Zrenjanin and the Municipality of Zagubica with support from the project prepared or updated their local economic development (LED) programs and employment plans to better foster women's entrepreneurship. In addition, a series of training were organized for women entrepreneurs, enhancing their skills in digital transformation, business plan preparation, and financial management.
During the first three years of this contribution and, to a great extent based on the experiences from MSPs, several tools have been developed. Some of them are: methodology for customer satisfaction with communal services (a pioneering effort in Serbia), methodology for developing waste management plans, developing research for mapping local policies (in order to develop practical policies), Guidelines for risk assessment and protections, Methodology for gender analyses for Gender responsive budgeting (another pioneering effort in Serbia), a tool for measuring the quantity and the morphology of waste. Several of these tools are based on Swedish municipal examples and they are all integral parts of the MSPs.

1) change of attitudes citizens are recognized as not just receivers of municipal services but active actors in the processes at the local level
2) improved skills municipalities learnt how to involve citizens in all the phases of developing local policy documents and action plan
3) change of practices local documents are revised to envisage mandatory participation of citizens, CSOs business community, in local planning and implementation of policies and action plans.
During the preparation of various MSP related plans, including Waste Management Plans, Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans, LAPs for gender equality, and LAPs for employment, citizens and CSOs were actively involved through surveys and direct consultations. This engagement also included focus group meetings with the private sector, schools, universities, elderly groups, NGOs, and other vulnerable populations.
Experiences and results from all MSP interventions are well documented and used in broader dissemination. As a result of this work, several publications have been produced for further and future use within municipal administrations but also other actors, such as public utility companies and CSOs.
